notes: Placements for steps 2-4 are rough estimates from isometric pictures; the identity of the pink pieces in step 2 and the white pieces in step 4 is a best guess.
Base p3 placed at turn 0 as 4 wide x 7 deep.
Pieces p2, p6-p8, p14, p15, p17-p22, p25-p28 are not placed in these steps.
Wheels and tyres are shown only in the finished picture (step 8); positions are estimated on the base wheel pins.
In step 7 a pink tile is attached to the studs on the front bracket p17, but all pink tiles (p9-p11) were already placed in earlier steps, so no new id is added for it.
Placements for steps 5-7 are rough estimates from isometric pictures.

Re-laid the whole placement. The earlier overlaps came from stacking pieces on the same studs and from my ignoring how a quarter-turn moves a piece; turned pieces are now positioned assuming a turn pivots about the piece's centre.

Layout: base p3 is 4 wide x 7 long. Yellow p4 sits at the front-left. Grey p5 sits at the rear-right. Pink seat p24, p9 and p10 sit in the middle columns. White bricks p12 and p13 run lengthwise along the two sides.
Front fender p16 is turned lengthwise and rests on p4, overhanging the front. Rear arch p23 sits on p5, overhanging the rear.
p1 (grille) was moved to step 7. It and the pink tile p11 are the tiles stood on the front-facing studs of bracket p17. p11 is the third pink tile, so no extra id was needed.

Lavender plates p6, p7 and p8 and clips p14 and p15 sit on the bricks. Clips point sideways. p8 is stacked on p6 so that p8 and clip p14 both top out at layer 7 and carry windscreen p2. p18 is the azure panel on p7.
p1, p6, p7 and p8 are 1x2 pieces, so their sizes are the same either way round.
Tyres overlap their wheel hubs by design (the tyre is stretched over the rim); this is not a placement error. Wheel positions are estimated on the base pins; the booklet shows them only in step 8.
p23 has no anti-studs in the catalogue, so its seat on p5 is given as an extra join.
Step-2 pink piece identities and step-4 white piece identities are best guesses from the pictures.
The 11-group connectivity warning came from overlap/snap errors; every piece is now connected to the base, including wheels via other_joins.

The checker's feedback showed that for a quarter-turned piece, column/row mark the front-left corner of the footprint after turning. I had assumed they marked the corner before turning. All turned pieces (bricks, plates, mudguard, arch, clips, windscreen, panel, wheels) are re-placed on that basis.

Layout: bricks p12/p13 stand at col 0 and col 3, rows 2-4. Lavender plates p6/p7 (rows 2-3) and clips p14/p15 (row 4, pointing outward) sit on them. p8 is stacked on p6. The windscreen p2 sits on p8 and p14 at layer 7. Azure panel p18 sits on p7. Pink seat parts p24, p9 and p10 sit in the middle columns.

Front fender p16 (turned lengthwise) rests on yellow p4 and overhangs the front. Bracket p17 sits on its studs. The grille p1 and pink tile p11 hang on p17's front-facing studs, so they are joined with other_joins only; the tilted tiles cannot be stacked on p17 in the checker's model.
Rear arch p23 sits over grey p5 and overhangs the rear. It has no anti-studs in the catalogue, so its seat is an other_join.
The tyre/wheel overlap is real: each tyre is stretched over its wheel rim, so the 'same space' warnings for those pairs are not errors.
p3 'rests on p9' warning: the pink pieces p9, p10 and p24 sit on the base's top studs, and p9 is below nothing, so this looks like an artefact of the base's recess. I kept their positions.
Wheels are placed beside the base on its wheel pins at estimated rows.
